summary: Usage dashboard appears not to count requests during onboarding (delayed usage aggregation) - customer believes API calls not being metered
body:
Issue summary
- Customer reports that after making multiple successful API calls during onboarding, the Usage dashboard in Redwood Console still shows $0 usage / 0 requests.
- Customer concern: “requests aren’t being counted” / “metering is broken” / may impact billing and quota behavior.

Customer impact
- Confusion during onboarding; customer delayed proceeding to production test because they believed calls were not registering.
- Risk: churn / low confidence in billing accuracy.

Customer report (verbatim excerpt)
- “We can see 200 responses from the API, but the console still shows 0 requests and 0 tokens. Is our account not tracking usage?”

Environment
- Hosted API (self-serve)
- Region: us-east
- Console: Usage tab + Project overview widgets

What we checked / hypothesis
- Hypothesis A: expected aggregation delay (usage dashboard ETL ~5–20 min, sometimes longer during backfill/partition catch-up).
- Hypothesis B: requests not attributed to the correct project (wrong API key / env var) -> common onboarding failure.
- Hypothesis C: telemetry freshness issue for us-east pipeline (delayed ingestion/transform), dashboard not showing latest partition.

Requested from customer
- Timestamp range of test calls (UTC)
- Request IDs and/or X-Request-Id headers
- Which API key / project was used
- Confirmation of console org/project they’re viewing

Current workaround
- Use request logs (if enabled) and response headers to validate calls are processed.
- Wait 15–30 minutes and refresh Usage dashboard (and ensure correct Project is selected).

Support goal for this ticket
- Confirm whether this is expected dashboard lag vs a metering attribution issue.
- If lag: communicate expected delay + open follow-up to add clearer UI messaging and data freshness indicator (ties to onboarding checklist work).
comments: 2025-03-12 09:18 (Priya Shah, Support) — Opened ticket from chat escalation. Customer sees successful calls but Usage dashboard still 0. Asked for timestamps + request IDs + confirmation they’re viewing correct project. Added note: this is showing up repeatedly in onboarding (similar vibe to SUP-18510/429 surprise and SUP-18421 auth issues).

2025-03-12 09:31 (BluePeak AI, Customer) — Calls were made around 09:00–09:10 UTC today. We used the API key from “Default Project” in the console. We don’t have request IDs saved, but we can re-run a call now if needed. Just want to confirm billing will reflect it.

2025-03-12 09:40 (Priya Shah, Support) — Replied to customer: usage dashboard can lag (typically 5–20 min). Asked them to re-run a single call and provide the X-Request-Id response header + exact UTC timestamp. Also confirmed they’re looking at the right org/project selector in Console. Shared a short workaround: check immediate response success + wait for aggregation window.

2025-03-12 10:02 (Priya Shah, Support - internal note) — Checked internal support dashboards: no obvious 5xx spikes on gateway for us-east. Seeing normal request volume. This looks like data freshness/ETL delay rather than request processing. Looping in Nadia (metering pipeline) for freshness checks. Also tagging Logan Wright for telemetry awareness.

2025-03-12 10:15 (Nadia Rahman, Telemetry/Metering) — Looking. We had a minor delay on the usage aggregation job (partition backlog) starting ~08:50 UTC due to an upstream warehouse throttling event. Job caught up by ~10:05 UTC. Data should be visible now or within next refresh. No loss expected. Will confirm with table partition timestamps.

2025-03-12 10:27 (Priya Shah, Support) — Updated customer: we identified a delay in the usage aggregation pipeline affecting the Usage dashboard; requests are still processed and will appear shortly. Asked them to refresh after ~15 minutes and confirm whether the numbers update. Reassured that metering is not lost; it’s a display/aggregation lag.

2025-03-12 10:44 (BluePeak AI, Customer) — Confirmed. Usage just updated and now shows tokens/requests. Thanks. Is this going to happen regularly? We were worried because it looked like nothing was being tracked.

2025-03-12 11:05 (Priya Shah, Support) — Responded: occasional delays can occur; typical window is 5–20 minutes. We’re improving freshness monitoring and adding clearer messaging in Console so it doesn’t look like “0 usage” means “not tracked.” Offered to share guidance for production: set budget alerts/quotas and rely on server responses for immediate validation. Closing once internal follow-up action items are captured.

2025-03-13 13:22 (Nadia Rahman, Telemetry/Metering) — Root cause: usage_agg hourly job experienced 58 min backlog due to warehouse throttling + retry delay; downstream Console uses latest completed partition, so UI shows stale snapshot (appears as 0 for new orgs with no prior partitions). No data loss. Suggest: add data freshness indicator + “Last updated at” timestamp on Usage page, and for new accounts show an onboarding callout: “Usage may take up to 30 min to appear.” Also add alert when partition delay > 20 min.

2025-03-13 13:30 (Priya Shah, Support - internal note) — This matches ongoing onboarding checklist project goals (reduce early confusion). Creating follow-up notes for Console/DevEx: add “Last updated” + banner for new orgs. Linking to PM-751 (TTFS/TTFP metrics validation) because dashboard lag also impacts onboarding metrics attribution if not accounted for.

2025-03-14 09:10 (Allison Grant, Observability) — +1 on freshness alert. Recommend thresholds: warn at 15m delay, page at 45m delay during business hours. Tie to onboarding funnel regression alerts in ENG-5815. Ensure alert routes to #eng-platform and #support when customer-facing.

2025-03-14 09:42 (Priya Shah, Support) — Resolution: confirmed metering correctness; issue was delayed aggregation causing stale Usage dashboard for a new account. Customer confirmed usage appeared. Captured follow-ups for data freshness alerting + Console messaging. Marking Resolved.
resolution: Confirmed this was a Usage dashboard data freshness lag (aggregation backlog) rather than missing metering. No data loss. Customer refreshed after pipeline catch-up and saw expected tokens/requests.
next_steps: Add a “Last updated” timestamp + data freshness messaging on Console Usage page (especially for new orgs/projects).
Implement pipeline freshness alerting for usage aggregation partitions (warn >15m, critical >45m) and route to on-call.
Document expected dashboard lag in onboarding checklist + troubleshooting (Support macros + docs).
Validate TTFS/TTFP metric computations account for known dashboard lag and do not use Console UI timestamps as the source of truth.
